clue.text: Ruthless tactics in difficult social gathering

parts.note: hard means difficult
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: Someone finds a tricky party tough going, with guests playing rough.
explanation.definitionFit: To play hardball is an idiom for using uncompromising, aggressive methods to get your way.

clue.text: Nag poor journalist?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a horse, especially a tired one hired out for riding
second meaning: a writer of dull, routine copy

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a sentence it seems to tell someone to pester a struggling reporter; the two phrases are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a worn-out riding horse and a mediocre writer turning out work for money.

clue.text: Defeat when Lancashire's No 9 gets dismissed

indicators.note: the number nine position picks the ninth letter of the county name before it

parts.note: taken as written
a batsman who is dismissed is out

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: Lancashire lose once their number nine batsman is out.
explanation.walkthrough: No 9 sounds like a cricket batting position, but it picks the ninth letter of the county's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing defeat, and as a verb it means to beat decisively.

clue.text: Like an idiot in cheerful group?

parts.note: blithe means carefree and happy
a ring is a group of people, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: One member of a jolly gang seems a bit of a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithering is an intensifying adjective for someone talking nonsense, as in a blithering idiot.

clue.text: Pine endlessly, coming to Cambridge city in need of company

indicators.note: the word for pine loses its final letter, its end

parts.note: to pine is to long for
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Someone yearns constantly on arriving in a fenland city where they know nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely describes someone sad because they are alone and want companionship.

clue.text: Fish stored in this cupboard

indicators.note: the letters are kept inside the words this cupboard, spanning both

parts.note: the fish's name runs across the end of this and the start of cupboard

explanation.surface: Someone points to a cupboard where a fish has been put away.
explanation.definitionFit: The scup is a porgy, a food fish of the American Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Study tragic Hardy girl, a noble female

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's tragic heroine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A literature student reads about Hardy's doomed heroine and an aristocratic lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Con meaning study is an old sense kept alive in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A contessa is an Italian countess, a woman of noble rank.

clue.text: Remorseful writer with intent to drop first name

parts.note: a pen is something to write with

indicators.note: the earlier of the two name letters in the word intent is left out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An author, sorry for something, means to keep their identity hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: Intent has two Ns; first tells you which one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone penitent feels sorrow and regret for wrongdoing, a synonym of contrite.

clue.text: Warnings — a count is fiddled

indicators.note: fiddled figures have been tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An alarm is raised because a tally has been falsified.
explanation.definitionFit: Cautions are formal warnings, such as a police caution given instead of a charge.

clue.text: Cathedral cleric will get caught out soon

indicators.note: the letter for caught is left out of the cleric's title

parts.note: a canon is a member of a cathedral chapter
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught on a scorecard

explanation.surface: A churchman will be exposed before long.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word for shortly or in a little while.

clue.text: One fixing "funny" part of the body for example

definitions.text: One fixing "funny" part of the body for example

parts.note: someone who sets things right, here a practitioner who mends the skeleton

parts.words: "funny" part of the body for example
parts.note: the funny bone is one bone of many, the elbow nerve that tingles when knocked

explanation.surface: A comic touch: someone fixes the body's funny part.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks flag that funny is not about humour: the funny bone is just one instance of what this person mends.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonesetter is a person, often unqualified, who resets fractured or dislocated bones.

clue.text: Most superficial son greeting old temptress Mae

parts.note: hallo is a variant of hello
Mae West was the sultry Hollywood star of the 1930s

explanation.surface: A young man says hello to a vintage screen siren.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallow means lacking depth of thought, so the superlative is the least profound.

clue.text: Had an influence as little devil, having done something

parts.note: an imp is a small demon or mischievous child
acted means took action

explanation.surface: A mischievous child made their mark by getting on with things.
explanation.definitionFit: Impacted is used as a verb meaning had an effect on something.

clue.text: Bugs in bear and cat, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone suspects their pets are carrying germs.
explanation.walkthrough: I fancy reads as I suppose, but fancy is the anagram signal and I is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs is an informal word for germs, the microbes that cause illness.

clue.text: Poor maiden meeting bore

parts.note: an eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up a river

explanation.surface: A sorry young woman is introduced to a tedious man.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over. Bore looks like a dull person, but it is the wave on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or inadequate, a synonym of poor in quantity or quality.

clue.text: For every boy there's somebody

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: Each lad has someone for him.
explanation.definitionFit: A person is an individual human being, which somebody also means.

clue.text: A quiet sheep in retreat

parts.note: taken as written
sh is the call for silence
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A silent animal is backing away.
explanation.walkthrough: Retreat looks like a verb for the sheep, but it is a noun naming a place of seclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious hermitage, a place of spiritual retreat.

clue.text: Surprised to see one imprisoned in Birmingham outhouse

indicators.note: the letter for one is locked inside the combined words for the place and building

parts.note: Aston is a district of Birmingham, home of Aston Villa
a shed is a small outbuilding

explanation.surface: Someone is startled to find a person locked in a garden shed in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston is an inner-city district of Birmingham, England's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonished means greatly surprised or amazed.

clue.text: In good health? Fancy that!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as an adjective, fit and healthy
second meaning: ... as an exclamation of surprise

explanation.walkthrough: A question followed by an exclamation seems like a conversation, but each part is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means healthy and also serves as an interjection, as in well, well, well.

clue.text: Catch sight of English agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: An instruction to spot a British secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is a literary verb meaning to notice or glimpse.

clue.text: Period in winter months

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words winter months, across the gap

parts.note: the period's name runs across the end of winter and the start of months

explanation.surface: A stretch of time during the cold season.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a fixed length of time, such as a school term.

clue.text: Monks having troubles — right to intervene

indicators.note: the letter for right comes between letters of the troubles word

parts.note: bothers is a verb meaning troubles or disturbs

explanation.surface: A monastery has problems, so the right thing is to step in.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a religious order call each other brothers, and monks are such men.

clue.text: Beloved costing a lot of money

explanation.walkthrough: Together the phrases suggest a cherished but pricey thing; they are two meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both affection for a person and a high price, as in a dear friend and a dear meal.

clue.text: A second gathering, regardless of ethical considerations

parts.note: taken as written
a mo is a moment, as in half a mo
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: A second mass meeting goes ahead without regard for right and wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorally describes acting without any moral sense at all, outside right and wrong.
